text: It is zero-allocation and shared by the player and bots, though only the player can stand on cover tops.

Measured on the real update() (tools/preview.js eval) and matched by integrating the same step: the jump apex depends on the frame rate, because tickVertical integrates gravity with the frame dt (:2537-2538): 2.25 / 2.43 / 2.48 m at 20 / 60 / 144 Hz, against 2.52 m from the formula. So the highest ledge a soldier can gain (apex + T.stepUp 0.55) is about 2.98 m at 60 Hz, while EJUMP_REACH assumes 3.07 m (:1575; the bots' jump test at :2932 and enemyClimbSteer at :1602, GN10). In v2 the reach follows from the fixed tick, and map validation (the EDITOR_V2 reachability panel, the LOOP_V2 §9 reachability check) must use the integrated value, not the formula. Not fully shared: only the player passes standOnCover (:2780, true); bots omit it (:2933), so only the player can stand on cover tops. v2 needs one rule for every soldier, since humans take over bot slots.

find: Avoid toggling material.transparent per mesh; a dither or stencil cutaway would fit WebGPU better and keeps merged meshes possible.
text: Avoid toggling material.transparent per mesh: on WebGPURenderer a blend-state change selects a different render pipeline, which may compile on first use (a spike measures the hitch). A cutaway computed in the shader from a world-space region between camera and player works on merged meshes. Which fade style (translucent, dithered or cut) is for the look brief.
Same system as GE1 (shamble-game.js:40-44; GE1 also covers the editor's Rules panel): count it once in the tally and keep one row as the owner (GE1 for the economy view, or merge the two).
